stem.en: A family has ₹30,000 to keep for five years at 8% a year, and two banks offer it differently. Bank A adds 8% of the original ₹30,000 at the end of every year. Bank B adds 8% of whatever the balance is at the end of that year. Both add the money to the account. Which statement about the family's total after five years is correct?

text.en: Bank A pays slightly more, because it adds a fixed ₹2,400 in every year, including the fifth year.
Both banks pay ₹42,000, because the same ₹30,000 is kept for the same five years at the same rate.
Bank B pays more than twice as much, because each year's interest is added to the rate as well as to the balance.
Bank B pays about ₹2,080 more, because its interest is charged on the growing balance and not on ₹30,000 every time.

explanation.en: Bank A pays ₹42,000 in all, after five additions of ₹2,400. Bank B pays ₹44,079.84, which is about ₹2,080 more. The difference appears from the second year onward: Bank A's ₹2,400 never changes, while Bank B's addition grows to ₹2,592, then ₹2,799.36 and so on, because it is charged on a larger balance each time. The rate stays at 8% in both banks, so nothing is doubled, and the fixed addition cannot pay more than the growing one.

hints.en: Work out both totals for two years first, and see where the two banks stop agreeing.
Bank B's first-year addition is ₹2,400, but its second-year addition is 8% of ₹32,400.
